item.title: South Carolina University issues all-clear after active shooter alert
item.description: The University of South Carolina issued and then lifted a shelter-in-place order Sunday evening following reports of a possible active shooter near the Thomas Cooper Library. Officials confirmed there was no gunman, attributing the alert to an abundance of caution after a video circulated online.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 2.2 million sign petition for Indian-origin trucker Harjinder Singh: Support grows for leniency; 45-year sentence looms
item.description: A petition with over 2.2 million signatures urges leniency for Harjinder Singh, an Indian man facing vehicular homicide charges in Florida after a fatal crash. Singh, who entered the US illegally in 2018, is accused of causing the death of three people. While some support leniency, citing it as an accident, others argue for equal justice.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘West blocking peace efforts’: Russian FM Sergei Lavrov defends Ukraine invasion; denies civilian targeting
item.description: In a rare interview, Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov defended Russia's actions in Ukraine, denying civilian targeting and accusing the West of obstructing peace. He questioned Zelenskyy's legitimacy, while Vice President JD Vance claimed Russia has made concessions to President Trump, including agreeing to Ukraine's territorial integrity. Diplomatic talks continue amidst accusations of delays and deadlock.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Flightmare: Passenger’s device catches fire on American airlines flight; smoke fills cabin, plane diverted
item.description: An American Airlines flight from Philadelphia to Phoenix had to land urgently. This happened because a passenger's electronic device caught fire mid-air. The flight landed safely at Washington Dulles International Airport. All passengers and crew were safe. The fire was quickly put out by the crew. Similar incidents involving devices catching fire on flights have increased recently.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Will send troops if needed’: Trump threatens Baltimore; slams Maryland governor Wes Moore over crime
item.description: Donald Trump has threatened to deploy federal troops to Baltimore, criticizing Governor Wes Moore's handling of the city's crime rates. Trump's statement follows similar warnings issued to New York City and Chicago, highlighting his "law and order" stance. He also suggested reconsidering federal aid for the Francis Scott Key bridge reconstruction, linking it to Baltimore's crime situation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Gerrymandering face-off: Hakeem Jeffries hits back at GOP; says ready for redistricting push in blue states
item.description: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries announced Democrats' readiness to counter Republican gerrymandering efforts in blue states, following Texas Republicans' redistricting moves. California has already responded, and further actions may occur if Republicans escalate their strategy. Despite redistricting challenges, Jeffries remains confident, citing past Democratic gains and focusing on healthcare and anti-corruption efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump’s letter of support to Ukraine : Calls for ‘negotiated settlement’; Zelenskyy vows ‘will not lose’ the war
item.description: On Ukraine's 34th Independence Day, global leaders, including Donald Trump, extended support amid the ongoing conflict with Russia. Trump lauded Ukraine's resilience and advocated for a negotiated settlement safeguarding its sovereignty. Volodymyr Zelensky affirmed Ukraine's resolve and self-respect. Other leaders like Xi Jinping, King Charles, and Mark Carney also conveyed their support.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Most effective way forward': Zelenskyy pushes for Putin talks as peace efforts stall; claims 'boots on Ukrainian ground important'
item.description: Zelenskyy wants direct talks with Vladimir Putin to end the war. He spoke as Ukraine celebrated its Independence Day. Celebrations happened amid drone attacks and ongoing battles. Russia rejected immediate meetings. Ukraine and Russia exchanged prisoners. Fighting continues in Donetsk. Both sides are far from a ceasefire after more than three years of war.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE confirms start of Rabi Al Awwal on August 25 after crescent not sighted
item.description: The UAE will begin Rabi Al Awwal on Monday, August 25, after the crescent moon was not sighted on Saturday. This marks a rare divergence from Saudi Arabia, which starts the month a day earlier. The Prophet Muhammad’s (PBUH) birthday will fall on September 5 in the UAE, possibly resulting in a three-day public holiday.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ukraine: Canada's Carney rules out Russian say on guarantees
item.description: During a visit to Kyiv for Independence Day, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called for an immediate ceasefire in Ukraine to halt the ongoing violence. Speaking alongside President Zelenskyy, Carney emphasized that Ukraine, along with its allies, should determine its own security guarantees, not Russia.

item.title: North Korea: Kim oversees 'new' missile test — state media
item.description: North Korea's Kim Jong Un oversaw the test firing of two new air defense missiles, showcasing their combat capabilities. This action occurred amidst rising tensions, including a recent border incident involving North Korean troops and ongoing joint military exercises between the United States and South Korea.

item.title: Emine Erdogan appeals to Melania Trump over Gaza's children
item.description: Emine Erdogan has urged Melania Trump to advocate for Gaza's children, appealing to her past advocacy for Ukrainian children. In a letter, Erdogan implored Trump to call on Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to end the humanitarian crisis. She highlighted the severe psychological distress of Gazan children, referencing the UN's reports of thousands of children deaths since the conflict began.

item.title: Israel strikes Houthis: Yemen's missile bases, area near presidential complex targeted; loud explosions reported
item.description: Loud explosions rocked Sanaa, Yemen's capital, on Sunday afternoon following reported Israeli airstrikes. A security source confirmed Israel's involvement, stating they carried out a strike in Sanaa. Residents reported the strikes targeted areas near the presidential complex and missile bases, with similar attacks reported in the port city of Hodeidah.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Florida truck crash: Family of Indian-origin Harjinder Singh urges mercy; driver faces 45-year prison term
item.description: Harjinder Singh, an Indian-origin truck driver, faces vehicular homicide charges in Florida after a fatal crash that killed three. His family pleads for leniency, while a petition supporting him gains traction. The case has sparked political debate, with concerns raised about potential discrimination against Punjabi truckers and visa restrictions.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Sweating and babbling’: British Airways flight attendant found naked and high on drugs mid-flight; probe under way
item.description: A British Airways flight attendant, Haden Pentecost, was discovered naked and under the influence of methamphetamine and amphetamines in an onboard toilet during a flight from California to London. His erratic behavior, including incoherent muttering and dilated pupils, prompted concern from the flight captain, leading to medical checks and hospitalization upon landing.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: How Abu Dhabi residents can get unlimited bus travel from Dh35 with Hafilat cards
item.description: Abu Dhabi offers unlimited bus travel through weekly and monthly passes. These passes are valid within Abu Dhabi city, Al Ain, and Al Dhafra. A seven-day pass costs Dh35, and a 30-day pass costs Dh95. Seniors and people of determination get subsidized monthly passes. Hafilat Smart Cards are needed to use these passes.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oman Golden Visa launch: Your path to business ownership and long-term residency
item.description: Oman is gearing up to launch a golden visa program. It aims to attract global investors. The program will also accelerate digital transformation in commerce. Alongside, the 'Al Majida Companies' initiative will support local firms. A digital system for commercial registrations will also be launched. These initiatives reflect Oman's efforts to modernize its economy and attract investment.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: UAE: Dubai Police opens new fully automated 24/7 Smart Police Station at Dragon Mart
item.description: Dubai Police has launched its 27th Smart Police Station at Dragon Mart, expanding its network of fully automated, 24/7 unmanned stations. Offering 45 services across criminal, traffic, certificates, and community needs in seven languages, these AI-driven stations boost digital transactions to 89.6%, cut energy use by 97%, save Dhs60 million, and significantly reduce carbon emissions.
